subject: general
question: For uniformly accelerated motion, which of the following is true about the velocity–time graph?

options.text: The graph is horizontal because velocity remains constant.
The graph is always curved because velocity changes irregularly.
The graph is a straight line because velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time.
The graph can have any shape depending on the motion.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The graph is a straight line because velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Uniformly accelerated motion** is defined as a type of motion in which the **velocity** of an object changes by **equal amounts** in **equal intervals of time**.
 
• In this type of motion, the **acceleration** remains **constant** throughout the duration of the movement.
 
• The **velocity-time graph** (v-t graph) for an object moving with **uniform acceleration** is always a **straight line**. This is because the relationship between velocity and time is **linear**, following the first equation of motion: **v = u + at**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The **slope** of the velocity-time graph represents the **acceleration** of the object. Since the slope of a straight line is **constant**, it signifies that the acceleration is **uniform**.
